newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jordan King to Gaza as PLO says talks in crisis.
newsitem.headline: Jordan King to Gaza as PLO says talks in crisis.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein due in self-ruled Gaza on Sunday for a meeting with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat as the Palestine Liberation Organisation appealed to the world to save peace talks "in crisis".

U.S. Middle East peace envoy Dennis Ross continued to press for an Israeli-PLO deal to launch self-rule in the West Bank town of Hebron even while the Palestinian Authority accused Israel of trying to scrap a 1995 interim peace deal.

"There is a crisis in the Israeli-Palestinian talks as a result of the Israeli insistence to reject adhering to signed agreements," the Authority said in a cabinet statement. "If the international community does not move immediately to save the peace process...then the whole region will witness explosions."

It said Israel's demand to delay by two years completion of planned troop pullbacks from rural areas of the West Bank areas violated a 1995 interim peace deal committing Israel to withdraw from most of the occupied territory by September 1997.
"The talks are close to a dead-end after the Israeli government has revealed its true positions and intentions towards the entire peace process," the statement said.
Palestinians have rejected an American compromise proposal that Israel complete further West Bank withdrawals by 1998.

In Jerusalem, Ross held late-night talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday after reporting no breakthroughs in earlier meetings with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and Palestinian negotiators in Cairo.
Seeking to bolster Arab support, Arafat was due to host Hussein and Jordanian Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti in Gaza on Sunday. Arafat held talks with Mubarak in Cairo on Saturday.
"This is part of the Jordanian-Egyptian-Palestinian consultation on the peace process," Arafat aide Nabil Abu Rdainah told Reuters.
The trip by King Hussein would be his first to the territoriy since Israel seized it in the 1967 Middle East war.

On a one-day trip to Paris at the weekend, Arafat urged French President Jacques Chirac to add a European impulse to Middle East peace moves. Arafat held talks with EU special envoy Jose Maria Moratinos upon returning to Gaza on Saturday.
Arafat's diplomatic flurry comes as Palestinian officials have grumbled of American "bias" towards Israel in the talks.
Ross said in Cairo a Hebron deal was "basically" complete but that other hurdles remained.
"We basically have resolved the Hebron issue," Ross told reporters in Cairo. "We have not overcome all the differences yet...we still have gaps on some of the non-Hebron issues."
Chief Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said he did not anticipate a quick resolution of the impasse.
"The main sticking point is not something easy. It is the nucleus of the interim agreement. It is the further redeployments," he told reporters in Cairo.

"I think the minute, the second, Mr. Netanyahu makes up his mind and gives his negotiator the green light to stick to the agreement signed in Washington...I think we will move to implement the outstanding commitments in the agreement."
Israel was due to have pulled out of most of Hebron, a volatile town of 400 Jewish settlers and 100,000 Arabs, last March. Violence and security concerns have delayed the pullout.
